https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinat.text:
Why do you love the US so much? As someone who has dedicated her career to telling stories about the States, it’s a question that I’m asked often — and it’s one with many possible answers. The simplest is: you could visit 100 times and no two trips would be the same.
The US is a continent mustering its best impression of a country. In a decade of travels in this big, beautiful, complicated nation, I’ve hiked in snow-crowned mountains, chased the sun on Pacific Coast beaches, museum-hopped in titanic cities, and had the best meals of my life in small towns you could blink and miss.
The country’s culture is every bit as diverse as its terrain and I relish cracking open a new slice of it each year. Most recently, a spry octogenarian taught me to flatfoot dance in the depths of Appalachia, while indigenous guides led me through the land that’s set to become America’s newest national park. I found one of the country’s finest art museums in the depths of the Ozarks (Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, in Arkansas, if you were wondering), and drank old fashioneds at breakfast in bourbon-soaked Kentucky. The only thing that no longer surprises me is how often the US surprises me.
This new year brings a renewed crop of reasons to visit — and with them, more fresh perspectives on a country that feels both warmly familiar and wonderfully exotic. Plan a 2025 trip to visit newly opened luxury hotels that are sure to become landmarks; attend art festivals on tropical islands; ride new rail routes; and celebrate pop culture anniversaries in style. Whether it’s your first, or your 100th, a trip to the US is always one worth taking.

In 2010 the Deepwater Horizon oil rig explosion caused devastation to the Gulf coast, painting the area’s beaches black and killing off wildlife from dolphins to sea turtles. Now, 15 years on, the region’s chalk-white sands are glittering again and the coastal city of Gulf Shores has put some resulting grant money to good use. Scheduled to open in the spring, the Gulf Coast Eco Center — near to the Lodge at Gulf State Park resort — will offer a dive into the region’s ecology, featuring exhibits, an art centre, hands-on family-friendly workshops, and a farm and garden.Details Seven nights’ room only from £1,250pp, including flights, car hire and accommodation at the Lodge at Gulf State Park (americaasyoulikeit.com)

Alaska has more shoreline than the rest of the contiguous US combined, so the best way to see this wild state is from the water. Opt for the indigenous-owned Alaskan Dream Cruises, a small-ship line that has launched two new expeditions for 2025. Most exciting is the eight-day Alaska’s Ultimate Adventure itinerary, which whisks guests from pretty southeastern Sitka, known for its Tlingit heritage, through the remote Inside Passage, to the quirky state capital, Juneau. The line’s vessels mean you’ll effortlessly navigate narrow waterways, striking deep into the heart of the Alaskan wilderness, while local naturalist guides will put your surroundings into context. Along the way test your legs with a hike in the Tongass National Forest; take a jet boat tour off Wrangell Island; and keep your eyes peeled for wildlife including grizzly bears, bald eagles and whales.Details Seven nights’ full board from £4,173pp, including all meals, excursions and airport transfers (alaskandreamcruises.com). Fly to Sitka via Seattle and Juneau
• Best cruises to see Alaska
When the sprawling VAI Resort opens in the desert town of Glendale this year, it’ll be the largest hotel in the state. That generous plot means room for 12 restaurants, including Bar Mar, a swish seafood spot spearheaded by the Spanish-American chef José Andrés, plus a giant six-acre pool. The extravagant resort even has a man-made island — sand-fringed Konos, with cabanas and a soaring aerial bar — and an amphitheatre with capacity for 11,000 people. It all backs on to the Mattel Adventure Park, a forthcoming theme park dreamt up by the toy conglomerate, featuring Hot Wheels rollercoasters, a giant Barbie dream house and Magic 8 Ball-inspired mini golf.Details Room-only doubles from £392 (vairesort.com). Fly to Phoenix
The small Ozarks town of Eureka Springs is an unexpected artistic hotspot: those in the know love its art galleries and one-off shops — not to mention its postcard-pretty mountain location. And it will get even more cultural clout this year with a brand new 300-seat opera house, soon to be home of the region’s prestigious Opera in the Ozarks programme, which has been running for more than 70 years. The theatre joins state cultural jewels including the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, in nearby Bentonville, whose mega expansion is tipped to finish in 2026 (it remains open during the works).Details Ten nights’ room only (including two in Eureka Springs and two in Bentonville) from £1,599pp, including flights and car hire (purelysouthernusa.co.uk)
Under Canvas has its tent pegs firmly in the ground at locations across the USA — and the glamping brand will make its California debut in the spring. Located in Groveland, in Tuolumne County, the latest offering drops you on the doorstep of the west entrance of Yosemite National Park, with its soaring granite peaks, waterfalls and wildflower meadows. The forested camp comes with creature comforts: generous, safari-style tents kitted out with rustic-chic furnishings, en suite bathrooms and locally sourced food at the restaurant that’s a serious step up from campfire beans. The season runs from May 15 to October 27.Details One night’s self-catering for two from £275 (undercanvas.com). Fly to Sacramento
• What to see and do in California
Keystone, west of Denver, draws winter sports lovers with its 3,000-plus acres of skiable terrain, lengthy season and family-focused attractions — and the brand new ski-in/ski-out Kindred Resort, tipped for a 2025 opening, will provide a luxurious base from which to enjoy it. Kindred takes après-ski seriously: there’s a planned bar, sushi spot and swish restaurant serving Colorado-inspired cuisine — plus a spa and pool to relax in after a day pounding the slopes. Rooms are chic and Alpine style — expect wooden accents, dark blue tweed and giant windows framing those snow-coated mountains.Details Room-only doubles from £257 (kindredresort.com). Fly to Denver

Foxwoods Resort Casino in Mashantucket — an hour’s drive from both Hartford and Providence — already has plenty for kids: an arcade, a zip line and go-karting, alongside the nightlife, spa and casino for adults. But come May the family-friendly offerings will be kicked up another gear with the opening of the Great Wolf Lodge waterpark. It will hinge around a colourful indoor centre with wave pools, twirling flumes and a lazy river, plus an adults-only hot springs area for unwinding. The new lodge will include more than 500 suites, including some log-cabin-themed spaces, plus a string of cheerful family-focused restaurants. Room rates include entrance to the new park.Details Room-only family suites from £195 (greatwolf.com). Fly to Hartford via Dublin
Delaware’s slice of the Atlantic shoreline is often overlooked by travellers, but it’s well worth exploring as part of an east coast itinerary. Its family-friendly resort towns offer good old-fashioned seaside fun — think piers, ice-cream parlours and miles of champagne-coloured sand. Among them, Rehoboth Beach deserves extra attention this year as it looks ahead to the opening of Belhaven Hotel. It’ll be an ideal coastal bolt hole, with a pool, breezy guestrooms and a stellar location right on the town’s Beach Boardwalk. Combine this jaunt with a stay in New Jersey’s Cape May, known for its Victorian architecture, and buzzy Atlantic City, accessible by car ferry over the Delaware Bay.Details Seven nights’ room only from £1,565pp, including flights and car hire (americaasyoulikeit.com)
The Sunshine State’s theme park portfolio will expand in the spring with the opening of Epic Universe at Universal Orlando Resort. It will feature five “lands”, from the cosmos-themed Celestial Park, featuring the Stardust Racers rollercoaster, to Dark Universe, a spooky plot filled with animated monsters and a werewolf-inspired ride. There are also areas dedicated to Harry Potter (including a fantastically detailed re-creation of the Ministry of Magic), the animated hit How to Train Your Dragon and Super Nintendo World. A new trio of hotels will debut too — the Mediterranean-inspired Universal Helios Grand Hotel and the glittering Universal Stella Nova and Universal Terra Luna resorts.Details Seven nights’ room only from £2,031pp, including flights and accommodation at Universal Helios Grand Hotel
• What else to see and do in Florida
Covering the traditional homelands of the indigenous Muscogee people, Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park spreads out in central Georgia, about a 90-minute drive from Atlanta. It’s a landscape of ancient and sacred grassy mounds, which are thought to have been built at least a thousand years ago. There’s also a replica Earth Lodge, an exhibit-packed visitor centre and guided tours that take a deep dive into the region’s Native history and culture. At present it’s a national historic park, but it’s gearing up to become America’s 64th full national park this year — a designation that would give the site extra protections and put it in the international spotlight.Details Thirteen nights’ room only from £2,935pp, including flights and car hire (bon-voyage.co.uk)
Most holidaymakers have their eye on Hawaii for its epic beaches, volcanic national parks and tropical climate — but the Pacific archipelago packs an artistic punch too. The Hawaii Triennial, a contemporary art exhibition focusing on creators from Hawaii and the Pacific Islands, returns for its fourth iteration. This year the showcase will highlight the work of 49 artists and will take place across venues on Oahu, Maui and Hawaii Island, marking the first time the event has expanded beyond Oahu. A trip also presents the opportunity to check out other cultural venues in Hawaii, from the artefact-packed Bishop Museum to the Shangri La Museum of Islamic Art, Culture and Design, both in Honolulu. Stay at the new Outrigger Waikiki Paradise Hotel in Waikiki, Oahu, built on a historic royal estate.Details Room-only doubles from £185. Fly to Honolulu
Idaho might just be the USA’s most underrated winter sports destination — but the 2025 Alpine Ski World Cup Finals, which is being held in Sun Valley for the first time (and in the USA for only the second time), will place the northwestern state in the limelight. The competition, from March 22-27, will attract the world’s top skiers. Once the day’s races are finished, the party will continue with the 5850 Festival in Ketchum, featuring live music and food and drinks vendors.Details Room-only doubles at Sun Valley Lodge from £941. Fly to Hailey, Idaho, via Salt Lake City
A new tour itinerary shines a spotlight on Illinois’ indigenous history and culture. Travellers will head south across the state, from Chicago to Edwardsville (just northeast of St Louis), with top stops including Hartford’s Lewis and Clark State Historic Site, which reveals the impact of early settlers on indigenous communities. Another highlight is Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site in Collinsville — a Unesco world heritage site whose large earthen mounds are echoes of an ancient civilisation and remain sacred to the region’s indigenous peoples (the site’s Interpretive Center is undergoing restoration work that may be completed by the end of the year). There’s also the Piney Creek Ravine State Natural Area, where leafy hikes lead to rare petroglyphs that could be more than 1,500 years old.Details Six nights’ room only from £1,298pp, including flights and car hire (americaasyoulikeit.com)
Indianapolis is home to the Indy 500 — one of the world’s great motor sports events — which is held annually at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and attracts plenty of Britons every year. This year the race, on May 25, will be complemented by the reopening of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum in April. Fresh-faced from a £70 million renovation, the museum will now feature seven permanent and three temporary galleries filled with motor sports relics — including jewels such as Nigel Mansell’s Indy Championship-winning 1993 Lola T93/00. The boutique Ironworks Hotel Indy, with its industrial chic design and string of bars and restaurants, is a 30-minute drive from the action. New flights from Dublin are launching in May too, so it’ll be even easier to reach America’s motor racing capital.Details Room-only doubles from £173. Fly to Indianapolis via Dublin
Plenty of US cities are celebrated for their contributions to American music — Nashville, New Orleans, Chicago, to name a handful. But fewer people might think of Clear Lake, in northern Iowa. Still, diehard music buffs will probably have heard of the Surf Ballroom, a history-rich venue that’s played host to music legends including the Big Bopper, Ritchie Valens and Buddy Holly, who played his last concert here. All that heritage is celebrated annually with the Winter Dance Party (Jan 30 to Feb 1), a tribute festival that celebrates the stars of the Ballroom’s heyday. Debuting in July, a new Music Enrichment and Immersive Center adjacent to the venue will take a deep dive into this slice of musical history. Explore on a tour that also visits cultural centres such as Des Moines, with its striking domed Capitol, and Iowa City, a Unesco city of literature.Details Twelve nights’ room only from £1,649pp, including flights, car hire and some extra meals (purelytravel.co.uk)
Billed as the first of its kind in the United States, the Museum of Art + Light debuted in the quirky college town of Manhattan, northeastern Kansas, in November 2024. It’s an extravaganza for the senses, combining contemporary artworks and classics from old masters with visual tech to create giant immersive displays. Debut exhibitions include Renoir: A Luminous Evolution, which features digital displays of paintings by the French impressionist, alongside personal family photographs and footage. There’s also an exhibition looking at the development of the digital arts and how it’s changing the creative world. Book a trip that packs in visits to Manhattan, the buzzy state capital, Topeka, and Wichita, plus Kansas’s Flint Hills, a precious area of tallgrass prairie.Details Eight nights’ room only from £2,455pp, including flights and car hire (bon-voyage.co.uk)

Kentucky’s Bourbon Trail stretches some 300 miles across the state, joining up key distilleries producing the whiskey that’s fondly nicknamed “America’s native spirit”. At the trail’s heart is Bardstown, the self-professed bourbon capital of the world and home to 11 distilleries, including the revered Bardstown Bourbon Company Distillery. Slated for an April opening, Bardstown’s new boutique Trail Hotel will be the perfect base from which to dive into bourbon country. Themed around the beloved spirit, the hotel will feature special touches including a bourbon lounge and in-the-know “bourbon butlers” who can book tours and tastings for guests.Details Room-only doubles from £148 (thetrailhotel.com). Fly to Louisville via Cincinnati
Launching this month, the new Spirit of Louisiana tour will join up four of the state’s most exciting cities. You’ll explore New Orleans landmarks such as cathedral-crowned Jackson Square and listen to live jazz in the genre’s birthplace — then it’s on to its capital, Baton Rouge, where the Old State Capitol building glitters like a Disney castle. Lafayette celebrates Louisiana’s rich musical tradition with its dancehalls swaying to Cajun and zydeco music. Meanwhile, Lake Charles has Gulf-fresh seafood, wildlife-rich swamp tours and the new Children’s Museum of Southwest Louisiana, which is poised to open in January.Details Ten nights’ room only from £1,910pp, including flights, car hire and some extra meals (americaasyoulikeit.com)
• Halloween in New Orleans with my teenage son
While the western half of the US has the lion’s share of America’s national parks, Acadia is the jewel of the east coast, drawing visitors with its pine forests, lighthouse-studded shores, lakes and meadows. You could spend days hiking, kayaking, stargazing and wildlife-watching — and from spring 2025 the Acadia Gateway Center should be visitors’ first port of call. The space will be filled with information on the park’s history, ecology and top hiking routes. It will also serve as a hub for the free Island Explorer — a shuttle service that whisks visitors through the wilderness, dropping them at popular trailheads and campsites. Tours combine adventures in Acadia with stops in New Hampshire’s North Conway (springboard for leafy Franconia Notch State Park) and Vermont’s cute capital, Montpelier.Details Eight nights’ room only from £1,930pp, including flights, transport and some extra meals

If you’re planning a big trip to Washington DC, it’s well worth slowing down and exploring a little more of the Capital Region — from historic wine regions and presidential homes in Virginia to Americana-rich small towns in Maryland. Frederick falls into the latter category — a quaint city less than an hour from both DC and Baltimore, stitched into a pretty landscape of mountains and wineries. Putting the small city on the map this year is the (aptly named) Visitation Hotel, the first new hotel in downtown Frederick for 50 years. It’s housed in a historic Catholic girls’ school, with stylish mid-century-inspired decor and a new restaurant from Top Chef’s Bryan Voltaggio.Details Room-only doubles from £220. Fly to Washington
Can you believe it’s been 50 years since Steven Spielberg terrified ocean lovers with his epic thriller about a giant killer shark? Massachusetts’ Martha’s Vineyard — a picture-perfect Atlantic island south of Cape Cod — was the setting for the fictional Amity Island, and the film’s anniversary will be celebrated in various ways. A new exhibition at the Martha’s Vineyard Museum (May 24 to September 7) will relive the movie drama with props, photos and stories from residents who remember when filming took place. While in town, make time for a Jaws tour too — Edgartown Tour Company (from £32; edgartowntours.com) offers an hour-long walking tour or a mega four-hour charter that relives scenes from the classic film. Make your base at the Harbor View Hotel, a grand seaside property that’s watched over Edgartown Harbor for more than a century.Details Room-only doubles from £176. Fly to Boston
Over the past decade once down-on-its-luck Detroit has been reimagined to the point of being unrecognisable: swish boutique hotels have filled vacant buildings, art has transformed alleyways and chef-led restaurants have inspired one of the Midwest’s most exciting food scenes. All eyes are on the dazzling Beaux-Arts Michigan Central Station: having been abandoned for decades, it had its grand reopening last summer and now offers tours, while a sprawling park is being built in its former rail yard. Change is afoot by the Detroit River too: this year will see the opening of the Ralph C Wilson Jr Centennial Park, with its water garden and lawn for concerts. Other anticipated debuts for this year include the HQ Detroit Hotel & Spa, a luxe spin-off of the Wyndham group that’ll be the first of its kind in the US, and a new Edition, downtown Detroit’s first five-star hotel. Meanwhile, you can’t go wrong with a stay in Shinola Hotel — the ultra-stylish property that kick-started the city’s boutique hotel boom.Details Room-only doubles from £220. Fly to Detroit
Just a handful of places in the Lower 48 offer the chance to see the northern lights — among them is Voyageurs National Park. Edging the Canadian border, the park is a world of forest-fringed inland lakes and wildlife-filled wetlands and it’s celebrating its 50th anniversary this year. The milestone will be marked with a series of soon-to-be-announced events, plus a new visitor centre at the park’s Crane Lake. Best of all, 2025 is expected to have increased and intense northern lights activity, so time your trip for winter for the best chance of a sighting. Combine your national park adventures with urban pursuits on a tour that includes Minneapolis–St Paul, quirky Duluth (birthplace of Bob Dylan) and lake-filled Itasca State Park.Details Thirteen nights’ room only from £2,995pp, including flights and car hire (bon-voyage.co.uk)
A passenger rail service hasn’t run along the US’s Gulf coast since 2005, when Hurricane Katrina caused severe damage to the track. Now, 20 years later, the long-anticipated Amtrak Gulf Coast route is finally set to return this spring. It’ll ease out from Mobile, Alabama — taking in the whole stretch of Mississippi’s Gulf coast with stops in Pascagoula, Biloxi, Gulfport and Bay St Louis — before finishing in New Orleans, Louisiana. Highlights of Mississippi’s sand-trimmed stretch include Ship Island, a history-steeped barrier isle accessible from Gulfport by ferry; Biloxi’s camera-loving lighthouse; and a bunch of cute coastal-inspired art galleries, one-off boutiques and seafood spots.Details Prices TBC (amtrak.com). Fly to Mobile and from New Orleans
• California to Texas on the USA’s unsung train trip
All eyes were on Kansas City last year, with Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce and the Chiefs’ Super Bowl victory propelling it into the spotlight. But this year it’s all about the state’s second-biggest city, St Louis. A series of openings will bolster the city’s attraction list, which already includes a great blues museum, Route 66 pitstops and the tallest arch in the world. Beeline for St Louis Union Station, a family-focused attraction with entertainment and dining that’s set to add a new mini rollercoaster and other rides. Then get a history fix at the landmark Old Courthouse (part of Gateway Arch National Park), whose multimillion-dollar restoration will finish in the summer. New galleries will explore the African-American experience in the city and the role of courts in US society.Details Sixteen nights’ room only from £2,769pp, including activities and some meals. Fly to Chicago
Montana’s winter sports scene is often overshadowed by famous resorts in Colorado and Utah — but an ambitious project named Big Sky 2025 is aiming to change that. Involving a total overhaul of Montana’s biggest and best-known resort, Big Sky, it will include the addition of new high-speed lifts and mega renovations of its existing hotels. Most exciting, and expected to open next year, is the new One&Only Moonlight Basin resort. Spreading out amid towering fir trees, the luxurious base will feature almost 100 ultra-chic cabins, rooms and suites, a Scandi-inspired spa and six restaurants including a Japanese-style steakhouse.Details B&B doubles from £750 (oneandonlyresorts.com). Fly to Bozeman via Denver
It might be easy to write off Nebraska as a flyover state — but its great plains are primed for some of the best birdwatching in the USA. About 80 per cent of the global population of sandhill cranes visit Nebraska’s Platte River Valley each spring and the National Audubon Society’s Rowe Sanctuary in Gibbon is the best place to witness the spectacle. Spring 2025 will mark the Sanctuary’s 50th annual crane season — it’s celebrating with a new visitor centre with exhibits, an education centre and a great hall featuring giant windows looking out onto the wilderness.Details Fourteen nights’ room only from £1,849pp, including flights, car hire and some extra meals (purelytravel.co.uk)
There’s always a flashy new attraction on the cards in Vegas and 2025 is no exception. This year will see the debut of what’s being called the Vegas Immersive District — a large development close to AREA15 that will be filled with entertaining things to do. Sure to be a crowd-pleaser, the chief attraction will be Universal Horror Unleashed, a permanent experience modelled on Universal’s popular but seasonal Halloween Horror Nights. There will be four goosebump-inducing haunted houses, with themes such as The Texas Chainsaw Massacre and The Exorcist brought to life with dizzying special effects, plus a whole range of spooky dining options. Beyond the perpetual Halloween drama, there’ll be new accommodation and shops. You are spoilt for choice with hotels on the Strip too: we love Vdara, a casino-free oasis with a top-notch spa.Details Room-only doubles from £86 (vdara.mgmresorts.com). Fly to Las Vegas

A new resort opening in spring 2025 will place you at the heart of the Lakes Region in central New Hampshire, an area that spreads south of the White Mountains, known for its farms, forests and spots to unwind by the water. The Lake Estate on Winnisquam resort spreads around the southwestern edge of its namesake, providing a base for adventures from paddleboarding to boating. That’s if you can tear yourself from the lodge. The decor takes inspiration from the natural surroundings, with wooden dressers, plant-stamped pillows and earthy blue and green accents. There will also be an inviting outdoor pool, a spa and an upmarket restaurant that will make the most of produce from local farms. An ideal New England escape that’s extra special when the region’s famous fall colours are blazing. Best of all, you’re just a 90-minute drive from Boston.Details Room-only doubles from £314 (thelakeestatenh.com). Fly to Boston
A stately new hotel has just opened in the unspoilt countryside of New Jersey’s Somerset County, right in New York City’s backyard. The Pendry Natirar is about 45 minutes from the heart of the Big Apple — though it’ll feel light years away. The leafy estate includes a lavish, Tudor-style mansion, plus the 66-room hotel, whose luxurious rooms, deluxe dining and glossy spa are everything you’d expect from the Pendry brand. Guests can also sharpen their culinary skills at a cooking school run by its restaurant, or try their hand at everything from archery to ebiking on the property’s 500 acres.Details Room-only doubles from £490 (pendry.com). Fly to Newark
It’s not hard to see how the Kasha-Katuwe Tent Rocks National Monument got its name. The rugged landscape rises and falls in a series of conical, tepee-like rock formations, shaped by volcanic eruptions that happened millions of years ago. The protected site also forms part of the indigenous Cochiti people’s traditional homelands and their culture is inherently connected to the site. The monument closed in 2020 due to Covid-19 and it has only just reopened. Now it is jointly managed by the Pueblo of Cochiti and the Bureau of Land Management, who have introduced new reservation systems to further protect the natural wonder. Spend time exploring the monument’s recreational trail, which reveals dramatic views of the rockscape and offers the chance to spot bird life from woodpeckers to warblers. A package tour combines a hike in the monument with New Mexico hotspots including Albuquerque, Carlsbad Caverns National Park, Santa Fe and the Bandelier National Monument.Details Fourteen nights’ room only from £1,999pp, including flights, car hire and some extra meals (purelytravel.co.uk)
It’s been 400 years since Dutch colonists sailed into Lenapehoking — homeland of the Lenape people, which would eventually become New York City. Diverse events marking the anniversary are planned throughout 2025 as part of the Future 400 programme, organised by the Netherlands Consulate General of New York (dutchcultureusa.com/future400). These should include colourful celebrations of the indigenous Lenape culture, such as artist workshops and dance performances, exhibitions of Dutch art and talks about the Dutch impact on New York. The programming for the separate, year-long NYC 400 Festival is yet to be announced, but will likely include concerts, public art and performances (nyc400th.com). Go all out and book a room at the newly renovated Waldorf Astoria in Midtown, which is poised for a spring opening. Or if you are planning an earlier trip, try Made Hotel in NoMad, with its trendy coffee shop, rooftop bar and boho-chic decor.Details Room-only doubles from £148 (madehotels.com). Fly to New York

While stellar art museums and solid food scenes (including some of America’s best barbecue) are reason enough to visit North Carolina, the cultured college town of Durham has something extra for 2025. The new Biscuits & Banjos festival (April 25-27) will lean into the region’s musical heritage, whose traditions include jazz, blues and bluegrass. It’s the vision of Rhiannon Giddens, from the Durham-originated string band Carolina Chocolate Drops, and will take place across urban venues including the historic Carolina Theatre. Stay downtown at the Durham Hotel, a boutique, mid-century-inspired spot that’s a short walk away from top museums, restaurants and festival venues.Details Room-only doubles from £148 (thedurham.com). Fly to Raleigh-Durham via Charlotte
North Dakota has natural wonders aplenty, from the rugged badlands of Theodore Roosevelt National Park in the state’s far west to the picturesque walking trails at Devils Lake in the northeast. This year the Pembina Gorge State Recreation Area will enter the limelight, as it’s developed into North Dakota’s 14th state park. The wild park swoops up towards the Canadian border and protects great tracts of oak forest, wildlife-rich wetlands and rugged bluffs that sink down towards the Pembina River. Spend time hiking, biking, horse riding and kayaking, and enjoying the new campgrounds currently under construction. Fly-drive tours beginning and ending in Fargo take in the best of the state’s outdoor attractions.Details Fourteen nights’ room only from £2,420pp, including flights and car hire (americaasyoulikeit.com)
There was a buzz about Oklahoma City in 2021, when the pioneering First Americans Museum opened, celebrating the history and contemporary culture of the state’s 39 tribal nations. Now an ambitious new resort will provide a base for exploring the museum’s inspiring exhibits (featuring everything from regalia to immersive retellings of the tribes’ origin stories) and offer plenty of family fun. Spearheaded by the Chickasaw Nation, the new, family-focused Okana Resort — whose name comes from the Chickasaw words “oka” (water) and “inkana” (friend) — will open next to the museum this year. It will include a massive indoor and outdoor waterpark (complete with 15 slides, a water coaster and a swim-up bar for adults), zip lines and laser tag, a spa and restaurants ranging from a cheerful burger bar to a Mexican street-food spot. You’ll be located on the Oklahoma River, a quick drive from the city’s Stockyards, the world-class Oklahoma City Museum of Art and the National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum. It’s the ultimate offbeat Wild West city break — or a stellar stop on a Route 66 itinerary.Details Room-only doubles from £195, including waterpark passes (okanaresort.com). Fly to Oklahoma City via Dallas
A city that leans into its eccentricities, Portland is best known for its cool one-off shops, quirky cultural scene, food trucks and brew pubs. But the opening of the luxurious Cascada hotel is likely to change the dial. Wellness is the property’s raison d’être and the hotel centres on a thermal springs spa with multiple pools, bespoke programmes and trending treatments such as HaloTherapy. All that serenity is continued in the rooms, which are soothingly minimalist with blackout curtains. You’ll also be located in the hip Alberta Arts district, in northeast Portland, so you can enjoy the neighbourhood’s street art, galleries and laid-back restaurants once you’re finished in the spa.Details Room-only doubles from £237 (cascada.me). Fly to Portland
• 9 of the best affordable hotels in Portland under £200
If you’re a national park lover, chances are you’ve gaped at geysers in Yellowstone, walked the rim of the Grand Canyon, and hiked before waterfalls in Yosemite. But have you ventured to Cuyahoga Valley National Park in northeastern Ohio? It’s just a 30-minute drive from Cleveland, but its rippling meadows, bird-filled forests and winding river will have you forgetting the buzz of the city in no time. The park was designated in December 1974 and 50th birthday celebrations that kicked off last month will continue into 2025. Plan a trip for special events such as concerts, nature and history talks, and adventures in the wilderness — including hikes on the Towpath Trail, which traces the path of the historic Ohio and Erie Canal. Make your base at the quaint 19th-century Inn at Brandywine Falls, whose namesake is one of the park’s natural highlights.Details Room-only doubles from £146 (theinnatbrandywinefalls.com). Fly to Cleveland via Detroit
Netflix is taking over the world. The streaming giant already has the power to glue the world to the sofa — and now it’s opening real-life experiences. Netflix House, planned for Philadelphia’s giant King of Prussia mall in the autumn, will feature immersive experiences themed around the service’s hit shows — from Stranger Things to Squid Game (it has teased the teeth-chattering glass bridge game) to Bridgerton (there’ll be a re-creation of the period drama set). Alongside the full-on entertainment, you can expect shops and restaurants inspired by your favourite series. The Alloy Hotel provides a base close to the action, with stylish communal areas and a chic modern American restaurant. (A second Netflix House will open in Dallas, Texas.)Details Room-only doubles from £96 (thealloyhotel.com). Fly to Philadelphia
Rhode Island may be America’s smallest state, but it offers a giant dose of coastal New England charm. Block Island, a beachy bolt hole accessible by ferry from Newport, is having something of a moment. The island already draws those looking for quiet with its sandy beaches, clifftop hiking trails, seafood restaurants and art galleries — and a host of new openings and renovations should attract even more visitors seeking seaside escapes. Newly launched tours are whisking visitors around the island by bike or ebike, drinking in lighthouses and ocean views, and offering the lowdown on local history (from £51pp; blockislandbiketour.com). Meanwhile, the Atlantic Inn, an elegant Victorian estate, is sparkling from recent renovations, while the ultra-chic Block Island Beach House (whose decor is coastal meets mid-century) has expanded too. Island-hopping package tours combine Block Island with Massachusetts hotspots Martha’s Vineyard, Nantucket and Cape Cod.Details Twelve nights’ room only from £2,350pp, including flights, car hire and some extra meals (pettitts.co.uk)
South Carolina’s top city already has charm aplenty — historic pastel-coloured rowhouses, a pristine riverfront and one of the South’s most robust restaurant scenes are all reasons to come. The 2023 opening of the International African American Museum cemented the city’s place on must-travel lists too. Now the landscape of the city is set to change with the opening of American Gardens, a new city park that will be laid out by the autumn. City-breakers will be able to escape into an oasis of crape myrtles, Spanish-moss-fringed live oak trees and fountains. It will centre on a grand lawn with a stage for live music and cultural events throughout the year. Book a few nights at Mills House Charleston, an elegant 19th-century property whose fountain-decorated courtyard, chic loungey restaurant and minimalist rooms offer a lesson in Southern charm.Details Room-only doubles from £226 (millshouse.com). Fly to Charleston via Charlotte
The four enormous presidential faces that look out from the Black Hills give South Dakota its nickname: the Mount Rushmore State. Mount Rushmore was designated a national memorial a century ago — and the sculptor Gutzon Borglum began carving work a few years afterwards, finishing the granite countenances of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln by the 1940s. Events will mark the 100-year anniversary in October 2025. However, the monument is controversial, sculpted into a landscape that’s sacred to the indigenous Lakota Sioux people. There are increased efforts to recognise Mount Rushmore’s impact on indigenous communities, including a 2023-launched tour from Trafalgar that dives into the region’s history and culture.Details Eight nights’ B&B from £2,995pp, including some extra meals, airport transfers and activities (trafalgar.com). Fly to Rapid City via Chicago
• The otherworld US states where cows outnumber humans
Few places are more intrinsically bound up with Elvis Presley than Memphis, where the rocker lived for most of his adult life. No surprise, then, that the city will be “all shook up” with celebrations for what would have been Presley’s 90th birthday (January 8). Things will kick off in January with live music and themed tours at Graceland, the quirky colonial revival mansion that he called home. If you can’t make it for the January celebrations, the Elvis 90 for 90 Exhibit, telling the King’s story through 90 of his personal effects, will last all year. There’s also Elvis Week in the summer (August 8–16), drawing fans for more concerts and talks, plus a candlelight vigil in honour of his life. The Peabody hotel is a Memphis institution — an Italian Renaissance-style jewel known for its resident ducks (which do a twice-daily march to the lobby fountain), sumptuous lobby bar and a string of celebrity guests.Details Room-only doubles from £157 (peabodymemphis.com). Fly to Memphis
• Elvis, Priscilla, Lisa Marie and the battle for Graceland• 8 best things to do in the Deep South
There are 26 Unesco world heritage sites in the US and among them is San Antonio’s string of 18th-century Spanish missions. They comprise the San José, San Juan, Espada and Concepcion Missions (all protected as the San Antonio Missions National Historical Park) and the Alamo, where the crucial Battle of the Alamo was fought in 1836 during the Texas Revolution. The missions’ aim was to assimilate the area’s indigenous peoples into Christian ways of life. This complex history will be explored at a new world heritage centre, set to open in February. The exhibit-filled space will introduce the missions and include displays on local art and culture. While in town, wander the Riverwalk and sample some of America’s best Tex-Mex too. The historic and luxurious Gunter Hotel will also be opening after renovations in the spring, offering a base right on the Riverwalk.Details Room-only doubles from £188 (thegunterhotel.com). Fly to San Antonio via Dallas
Park City, a pretty ski town about an hour southeast of Utah’s Great Salt Lake, purports to have the “greatest snow on Earth” — and there may be some truth in this fancy. A complex meteorological phenomenon called the “lake effect” results in heavy snowfall of the dry, light kind that’s just right for skiing. Happily, there’ll be even more space to enjoy this perfect powder for the 2025/26 ski season. The family-friendly Deer Valley resort is in the throes of a vast expansion that will more than double its size. Winter sports lovers can take to the 3,700 acres of skiable terrain that have been added, hang out in a buzzy new ski village, and lean into après-ski culture with plenty of restaurants and shops. The resort’s newest lodging, Grand Hyatt Deer Valley, is the place to stay.Details Room-only doubles from £612 (hyatt.com); lift passes from £189 per person, per day (deervalley.com). Fly to Salt Lake City
The tiny town of Stowe smacks of New England charm — right down to its perfect white steepled church and its burnt foliage in the autumn. It’s also a fine base for winter sports, including skiing, fat biking and snowmobiling. Now a flurry of new accommodation and recent hotel renovations are boosting Stowe’s credentials as a New England holiday hotspot. Check into just-opened AWOL (by Lark Hotels), a Scandi-inspired bolt hole on Stowe’s forested fringes with fire pits and a library. Or spend a winter break at the Lodge at Spruce Peak, a luxury ski resort that’s been updated with treehouse accommodations and a new taqueria. Another trendy outpost is Outbound Stowe, which includes cottages, cabins and suites, plus a large outdoor pool.Details B&B doubles from £132 (larkhotels.com). Fly to Burlington via Boston
Hear the phrase “country music” and Nashville probably springs to mind — but did you know that the real birthplace of the genre lies a little further east of Tennessee’s song-soaked capital? Bristol, a small city that straddles the Tennessee and Virginia border, was the host of the “Bristol Sessions” — a series of 1927 recordings from early legends such as the Carter Family and Jimmie Rodgers. Those sessions are often called the “big bang” of country music. Today the Smithsonian-affiliated Birthplace of Country Museum tells the story of the genre’s nascence, while the popular Bristol Rhythm & Roots Reunion festival draws international Americana music fans (September 19–21). Now the newly opened Hard Rock Hotel & Casino is cementing Bristol’s place on the map — the venue will host a full roster of live events for 2025, from concerts to comedy gigs. Rent a car to explore more of southwest Virginia’s Crooked Road, a heritage trail that joins up the museums and historic venues that tell the state’s musical story.Details Room-only doubles from £95 (hotel.hardrock.com). Fly to Roanoke via Washington DC
The 1 Hotels brand has been taking the States by storm and an opening is a sure sign that a city’s luxury scene is on the up. Newest in the mix is Seattle’s very own iteration, a reimagining of the already chic Denny Park Hotel. In keeping with 1 Hotels’ other spots in New York and London, the Emerald City opening will centre on wellness and sustainability — think interiors clad with reclaimed wood and living walls, a sleek fitness centre, and a restaurant whose menu is built on seasonal produce from the Pacific Northwest. The location sings too: the hotel will land you in the South Lake Union neighbourhood, a trendy tech hub that buzzes with bars and restaurants, and offers fabulous views across downtown Seattle.Details Room-only doubles from £317 (1hotels.com). Fly to Seattle
West Virginia might just be the most underrated place for nature lovers in the US. This bucolic slice of Appalachia promises hikes to thundering waterfalls; gaping gorges carved out by ancient waterways (New River Gorge became America’s latest national park in 2020); and forests laced with trails. All that wilderness means some extra-dark skies too — and that’s true of Coopers Rock State Forest, in the state’s far north near Morgantown. Folded into the forest and bookable from 2025 will be a new string of stargazing cabins, complete with telescopes. Spend the rest of your time hiking, biking and drinking in the views from soaring canyon viewpoints. Opt for a tour package that highlights more Mountain State wonders, including Blackwater Falls State Park and the historic spa city of White Sulphur Springs (home of the grand Greenbrier resort).Details Fourteen nights’ room only from £2,199pp, including flights and car hire (purelysouthernusa.co.uk)
Bordering mighty Lake Michigan and Lake Superior, and filled with forests, rivers and inland lakes, Wisconsin is well primed for outdoor pursuits. One adventure hotspot is Wisconsin Dells, which perfectly pairs family fun with outdoor adventure and has been visited by US holidaymakers since the mid-1800s. It’s known for its location on the Wisconsin River and dramatic sandstone bluffs, best explored with dreamy hikes and boat rides. Meanwhile, its huge concentration of waterparks (it claims to have more per capita than anywhere on Earth) has earned it the trademarked nickname Waterpark Capital of the World. New for 2025 is the Kalahari Treehouse Collection at the family-focused Wisconsin Dells Resort. The luxurious lodgings promise plenty of creature comforts and views over pretty Lake Delton, while a new supper club will make the most of the region’s bountiful produce. You’ll also have free access to the resort’s very own indoor waterpark. Spend a few days enjoying the accommodations on a tour that includes more Wisconsin jewels, such as picturesque Bayfield, alongside time in cities including Chicago, Illinois, and Minneapolis, Minnesota.Details Thirteen nights’ room only from £2,995pp, including flights and car hire (bon-voyage.co.uk)
Through the late 1800s and early 1900s, wolves — which were seen as a threat to the region’s livestock — were hunted to extinction in Yellowstone National Park. Many decades passed with these majestic predators absent from Yellowstone’s epic backyard and they were eventually placed on the Endangered Species Act list across 48 states. The tides turned in 1995, when wolves were reintroduced to the park as part of a painstaking conservation programme. Now, the population numbers about 120 and that fact will be celebrated through 2025, 30 years on. Book the Winter Wolf Discovery Package through Yellowstone National Park Lodges — you’ll stay at the cosy Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel and spend your days embarking on road trips and snowshoe treks, in search of wolves and other wildlife including moose and bears.Details Four nights’ B&B from £1,405pp, including some extra meals, in-park transport and wildlife excursions (yellowstonenationalparklodges.com). Fly to Cody via Denver
This year the US capital will host World Pride (May 17 to June 8; worldpridedc.org), a jubilant celebration of love and freedom that takes place in a new city every couple of years. The festivities also coincide with the 50th anniversary of DC’s own annual citywide pride celebrations. Visitors can expect live music (including a headlining performance from the Colombian megastar Shakira), parades filled with rainbow-coloured floats and flags, street vendors, a film festival and endless food and drink. DC’s hotel scene is buzzing, so you’ll have no trouble finding a base near the action: top spots include the Darcy Hotel in Logan Circle Kimpton and Hotel Monaco in the Penn Quarter.Details Room-only doubles from £174 (monaco-dc.com). Fly to Washington DC

https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/.title: Shell faces shareholder revolt against scrapped climate targets
https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/.subtitle: Pension funds object to the energy group’s decision to grow its liquefied natural gas business
https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/.text:
A showdown with investors looms for Shell after three local government pension funds urged the energy group to explain an “apparent disconnect” between plans to increase gas production and a goal to hit net zero by 2050.
The Merseyside Pension Fund, Greater Manchester Pension Fund and Brunel Pension Partnership have filed a shareholder resolution calling on the FTSE 100 oil major to justify how a target to grow its liquefied natural gas business by up to 30 per cent by the end of the decade, compared with 2022 levels, is compatible with emissions reduction targets.
At the latest update of its transition strategy last year Shell watered down a 2030 carbon reduction target and scrapped a 2035 carbon intensity reduction objective, citing expectations of strong demand for gas and uncertainty about the energy transition.
It is aiming to reduce its carbon intensity by between 15 and 20 per cent by 2030, a measure that presents emissions as a proportion of all the energy the company sells, which allows Shell to offset carbon produced by oil and gas operations against the less polluting parts of the business. It has reaffirmed plans to cut emissions to net zero by 2050.
Vaishnavi Ravishankar, head of stewardship at Brunel Pension Partnership, said it was “deeply concerned” about the apparent inconsistency between Shell’s LNG growth strategy and its stated climate targets.
“We need to see further transparency to assess Shell’s alignment with climate goals, particularly in the context of the recent removal of its interim 2035 climate target. We are committed to engaging with Shell to enhance the ambition, transparency, and credibility of its climate transition efforts,” Ravishankar said.
The pension schemes, which manage about £69 billion in assets, have also questioned the strength of demand for LNG projected by Shell over the next 15 years.
The group, which is the world’s largest trader of LNG, has forecast an increase of more than 50 per cent by 2040, which the shareholders argue is built on an anticipated level of demand higher than every scenario put out by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and appears to have “misinterpreted independent analysis in substantiating its demand projections”.
The resolution has been filed by the shareholders, which have an aggregate stake of 0.3 per cent in the company, before its annual meeting in May.
A spokesman for Shell said that shareholders had “strongly backed” its strategy “to deliver more value with less emissions at successive AGMs, with the growing role of LNG at the heart of this strategy”.
“We are confident in the future role of LNG in our strategy, as we transform to become a net zero emissions energy business by 2050,” he said.
Wael Sawan, chief executive of Europe’s biggest oil and gas group, is due to update investors on its strategy in March for the second time since he was appointed at the start of 2023.
The resolution has been co-filed with the Australasian Centre for Corporate Responsibility and is supported by Share Action, the campaign group, as well as 100 individual shareholders, the investors said.
